## Summary
A numeric gates rubric — "How to clean up AI slop in your codebase":

- Cyclomatic Complexity < 22
- Cognitive Complexity < 22
- Halstead Difficulty < 80
- Lines of Code per File < 500
- Test Coverage: 100%
- CRAP < 25
- Surviving mutants: 0
- Dead code: 0
- Redundant code: 0
- `any` / `unknown` types: 0

Stats at capture: 246.7k views, 2.7k likes, **5.5k bookmarks** (bookmarks ≈ 2× likes — a saved-as-working-rubric signal), 95 RTs, 68 replies.

## Why it matters
- Turns "is this code slop?" from a vibe into a checklist: complexity (cyclomatic / cognitive / Halstead), file size, coverage, change-risk (CRAP), mutation testing, and dead / redundant / loose-typing hygiene — each with a number.
- The strict end (100% coverage, 0 surviving mutants) is aspirational for AI-generated code; the value is having explicit thresholds to ratchet toward, not hitting all ten on day one.
- Pairs with tooling that automates the gates — the cyclomatic-complexity skill already covers gate #1.
